w-th-008.title: Tapioca Coconut Mini Cookies (Khanom Phing)

instructions.1: Combine coconut milk, sugar, and pandan leaf in a heavy-bottomed pot and simmer for about 25 minutes, stirring occasionally until it has a thick syrupy consistency (it will thicken more as it cools).
instructions.2: Remove the pandan leaf and let the syrup cool until it's lukewarm, then stir in the egg yolk. If you want to colour the dough with only one colour, add the food colouring at this point.
instructions.3: Place the tapioca starch in a large mixing bowl, make a well in the center, and pour in the coconut syrup. Knead the dough together until it's smooth. If the dough feels very dry, add a little water at a time. If the dough feels too soft, add a little more tapioca starch.
instructions.4: If you want to colour the dough with different colours, split the dough into portions and knead in food colouring until the colour is smooth.
instructions.5: Let the dough rest for 30 minutes covered in plastic wrap to prevent it from drying out.
instructions.6: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F).
instructions.7: Form the dough into small balls and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper or a silicone liner. You can also generously grease the baking sheet with coconut oil.
instructions.8: Bake the cookies in the oven for 25-30 minutes or until the bottoms are slightly browned. You can bake one tray at a time for consistency, or if you bake two trays at once, switch their positions halfway through the baking process.
instructions.9: Once the cookies are done, turn off the oven and open the oven door for about 8 seconds to drop the temperature, then put the cookies back in and let them cool in the warm oven. This step is optional but recommended to dry out the cookies completely and improve the texture.
instructions.10: Once cooled, store the cookies in an airtight container and enjoy!

w-th-008.culturalNotes: Khanom Phing is a traditional Thai dessert known for its rich coconut flavor and light, fluffy texture.

w-th-009.title: Khanom Thuai

instructions.1: Mix the rice flour and brown sugar in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Add the milk and vegetable oil and mix well until the batter is smooth.
instructions.3: Add the cinnamon and cloves and mix again.
instructions.4: Add the raisins and walnuts and mix them well into the batter.
instructions.5: Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat.
instructions.6: Pour a tablespoon of the batter into the pan and spread it gently.
instructions.7: Cook the pancake until it is golden brown on the bottom, then flip and cook the other side.
instructions.8: Repeat the process until all the batter is used.
instructions.9: Serve the pancakes hot or cold as desired.

w-th-009.culturalNotes: Khanom Thuai is a traditional Thai dessert often served on special occasions.

w-th-010.title: Khao Soi: Northern Thai Curry Noodle Soup

instructions.1: In a pan, toast the black cardamom pods and coriander seeds over medium heat until golden and fragrant. Grind them in a spice grinder.
instructions.2: In a bowl, mix the ginger, fresh turmeric, sliced shallots, dried chilies, salt, and curry paste.
instructions.3: In a large pot, add the coconut milk, water, soy sauce, black soy sauce, fish sauce, and palm sugar. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the chicken drumsticks to the pot and cook for 20 minutes or until fully cooked.
instructions.5: In another bowl, rinse the fresh egg noodles and soak them in hot water for 5 minutes. Drain the noodles and divide them into portions.
instructions.6: In a serving bowl, place the noodles, top with the cooked chicken, and pour the broth over them. Serve with chopped cilantro, green onions, lime wedges, chopped shallots, pickled mustard greens, and fried chili flakes as desired.

w-th-010.culturalNotes: Khao soi is a popular dish in northern Thailand, known for its rich curry broth and coconut milk flavor.

w-th-011.title: Mango Sticky Rice

instructions.1: Rinse the glutinous rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear.
instructions.2: Soak the rice in water for 30 minutes, then drain it.
instructions.3: Place the rice in a pot with 1 cup of water and bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes until the rice is tender.
instructions.4: In a small saucepan, mix ⅔ cup of coconut milk with ½ teaspoon of salt and ½ cup of sugar. Heat over low heat until the sugar dissolves.
instructions.5: In another small saucepan, mix ½ cup of coconut milk with ¼ teaspoon of salt, 1 teaspoon of rice flour, and 1 Tablespoon of water. Heat over low heat until the mixture thickens.
instructions.6: In a frying pan, fry the mung beans until golden brown.
instructions.7: Slice the mangoes into thin slices.
instructions.8: Serve the sticky rice with the mango slices, the salted coconut sauce, and the fried mung beans.

w-th-011.culturalNotes: Mango sticky rice is a popular dessert in Thailand, often served on special occasions.

w-th-012.title: Beef Massaman Curry

instructions.1: Cut the beef off the bones and, if necessary, cut them down into large cubes.
instructions.2: In a heavy-bottomed pot, add just enough oil to coat the bottom and heat over medium-high heat until very hot. Sear the beef in the oil until well browned on 2 sides (or 3-4 sides if you have the patience). Do this in as many batches as necessary.
instructions.3: Once all the beef is seared, add it all back into the pot, along with the bones you removed.
instructions.4: Add 1/2 cup of coconut milk and just enough water to keep everything submerged. Add 1 Tbsp of the curry paste and 1 Tbsp fish sauce, and simmer gently for 2-2.5 hours or until the beef is fork-tender. Set it aside.
instructions.5: In another heavy-bottomed pot (this will be your curry pot), add about 3/4 cup of the remaining coconut milk and bring to a boil. Let it boil until reduced by about half, and the coconut milk looks significantly thicker.
instructions.6: Add the remaining curry paste and sauté it in the coconut milk over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the coconut oil separates from the paste (it will start to sizzle around the edges of the paste). If the paste sticks to the pot before it is ready, you can deglaze with a splash of the remaining coconut milk as needed.
instructions.7: Once the paste is ready, add the remaining coconut milk and stir to dissolve the paste. Add 1 Tbsp of the fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind juice.
instructions.8: Using tongs, remove the beef from the braising liquid and add it to the curry pot, saving the cooking liquid. (Do not add the bones back in unless there's still meat on it that you want to eat.) Then add the onion, sweet potato, and peanuts to the curry.
instructions.9: Skim off the fat and scum from the beef cooking liquid, then add just enough of the liquid to the curry to keep everything submerged.
instructions.10: Bring the curry to a simmer and let it cook gently for another 10-15 minutes until the sweet potatoes are fork-tender.
instructions.11: Taste the curry and adjust the final seasoning with more fish sauce, sugar, or tamarind as needed. This is very important because everyone will end up with a different amount of salt at this point depending on the saltiness of your curry paste and also how much cooking liquid you end up adding. So, taste.
instructions.12: Serve the curry with jasmine rice. Enjoy!

w-th-012.culturalNotes: Massaman curry is a traditional Thai dish that blends Thai and Arabic flavors. It is known for its sweet, sour, and salty taste.

w-th-013.title: Miang Kham

w-th-013-i4.name: dried shrimp
w-th-013-i4.standardAmount: 1/3 cup (soaked in hot water for 15 minutes)

w-th-013-i13.name: shrimp paste
w-th-013-i13.standardAmount: 1 teaspoon (or more if you like the flavor)

instructions.1: In a blender, blend the dried shrimp until fine, then add the galangal, ginger, and about half of the water and blend until smooth.
instructions.2: Pour the mixture into a small pot. Rinse the blender with the remaining water and pour it into the pot.
instructions.3: Add palm sugar, shrimp paste, and fish sauce to the mixture, then bring to a simmer until the sugar is completely dissolved.
instructions.4: After the sugar has dissolved, reduce the heat and simmer for 5 more minutes until the mixture thickens.
instructions.5: Add the ground coconut and ground peanuts. Let the sauce cool until it's lukewarm, then check the consistency to make sure it is not too thick. If it is, you can add a bit more water. If it's too runny, reduce it a bit more.
instructions.6: To eat the wrap, make a little cone with the betel leaf, then fill it with all the wrap ingredients to your liking. Top with a little bit of sauce, close the cup and eat it all in one bite!

w-th-013.culturalNotes: Miang Kham is a traditional Thai dish served as an appetizer. It is often presented at social gatherings and parties.

w-th-014.title: Grilled Steak Salad (Nam Tok Neua)

instructions.1: Combine all steak marinade ingredients in a bowl and stir until the sugar is dissolved. Place the steak in a sealable plastic bag or in a container that isn’t much bigger than the size of the steak, then add the marinade and toss to coat the steak all over. Marinate for at least 2 hours and up to overnight, turning the steak at least once in between to redistribute the marinade.
instructions.2: If refrigerated, bring the steak out to room temperature at least 30 minutes before grilling. Grill the steak in a closed preheated barbecue over medium-high heat (400°F/200°C) for 6 to 8 minutes for medium doneness. Turn the steak at least twice, or every 1.5 minutes or so, for more even cooking.
instructions.3: Remove the steak from the grill and let it rest on a plate for at least 5 minutes, keeping all the liquid that pools on the plate.
instructions.4: While the steak rests, make the toasted rice powder by adding the rice and the makrut lime leaf (if using) to a dry skillet and cook over high heat, stirring constantly until the rice has developed a dark brown color, or about 3-4 minutes. Pour the rice and lime leaf onto a plate to cool slightly, then grind into a powder using a mortar and pestle or a coffee grinder.
instructions.5: Once the steak has rested for at least 5 minutes, thinly slice it into bite-sized pieces and add to a medium mixing bowl along with any of the collected steak juices. Add 1 tablespoon (15 ml) of the water or stock, plus the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, chili flakes, and the toasted rice powder; toss to mix well.
instructions.6: Add the lemongrass, shallots, mint, cilantro, and sawtooth coriander (if using) and toss to mix. Taste, and if the flavor feels a little too salty, add the remaining water or stock to dilute. Serve immediately with Thai sticky rice.

w-th-014.culturalNotes: Nam Tok Neua is a popular dish in Thailand, served as a grilled steak salad with traditional Thai spices.

w-th-015.title: Indonesian Fried Rice (Nasi Goreng)

w-th-015-i1.name: jasmine rice
w-th-015-i1.standardAmount: 2.5 cups (cooked according to package instructions and refrigerated overnight)

instructions.1: Cook the rice according to the package instructions and refrigerate it overnight.
instructions.2: The next day, heat the oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat.
instructions.3: Add the garlic and chili pepper (if using) and cook until soft and beginning to brown.
instructions.4: Add the kecap manis and the cooled rice, breaking up any clumps as needed. Fry the rice while stirring.
instructions.5: When the rice is evenly coated with the sauce and a little crispy, it's done cooking.
instructions.6: Serve the nasi goreng with cucumber, green onion, and tomatoes.
instructions.7: Make one egg per person (the cow's eye) and serve it with the rice.

w-th-015.culturalNotes: Nasi Goreng is a popular dish in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, and is typically served as a breakfast or dinner meal.

w-th-016.title: Malaysian Nasi Lemak

instructions.1: Rinse the rice and drain it. Add coconut milk, a pinch of salt, and water as needed.
instructions.2: Add the knotted pandan leaves to the rice and cook until tender.
instructions.3: Rinse the dried anchovies and drain the water. Pat them dry and fry until golden brown, then set aside.
instructions.4: Using a mortar and pestle, pound the prawn paste with the shallots, garlic, and seeded dried chilies.
instructions.5: Slice the red onion into rings.
instructions.6: Soak the tamarind pulp in water for 15 minutes. Squeeze the pulp constantly to extract the flavor into the water. Drain the pulp and save the tamarind juice.
instructions.7: Heat some oil in a skillet and fry the paste until fragrant.
instructions.9: Add the fried anchovies and stir well.
instructions.10: Add the tamarind juice, salt, and sugar.
instructions.11: Simmer on low heat until the sambal thickens. Set aside.
instructions.12: Clean the small fish, cut them in half, and season with salt. Deep fry them.
instructions.13: Serve the steamed coconut rice on a banana leaf and pour some of the sambal over the rice.
instructions.14: Serve with fried fish, cucumber slices, hard-boiled eggs, peanuts, and more fried anchovies.

w-th-016.culturalNotes: Nasi Lemak is the national dish of Malaysia, typically served on a banana leaf with a variety of complementary ingredients.

w-th-017.title: Panang Curry Beef

instructions.1: Grind the cumin and coriander seeds until very fine using a mortar and pestle or a coffee grinder.
instructions.2: Add roasted peanuts and grind until fine.
instructions.3: Mix the red curry paste and shrimp paste into the ground spice mixture.
instructions.4: Add fish sauce and oil to beef and massage it in with your hands, separating the pieces of beef that are stuck together as you mix.
instructions.5: In a saute pan or a wok over medium high heat, reduce ¾ cup coconut milk until thickened and creamy.
instructions.6: Stir in curry paste and reduce the heat to medium low. Cook the paste for a few minutes, stirring constantly, until coconut oil separates away from the paste. If the paste sticks to the pan, you can deglaze with a bit of the remaining coconut milk.
instructions.7: Add palm sugar and torn kaffir lime leaves and cook for a minute or so until the sugar is dissolved.
instructions.8: Add beef and quickly toss it with the curry paste, separating the pieces of beef as much as you can. Once the beef is about 50% cooked, add the remaining coconut milk and stir for 30 more seconds or just until the beef is fully cooked. If it looks too dry, you can add a splash of water at this point.
instructions.9: Stir in red peppers, if using, and turn off the heat.
instructions.10: Taste and adjust seasoning with more fish sauce and/or sugar as needed.
instructions.11: Garnish with julienned kaffir lime leaves and more red peppers as desired.

w-th-017.culturalNotes: Panang curry is a traditional Thai dish known for its rich flavors and sweet-salty taste.

w-th-018.title: Custard in a Pumpkin

instructions.1: Wash the pumpkin thoroughly and cut off the top. Gently scoop out the seeds and inner skin.
instructions.2: Add coconut milk, palm sugar, rice flour or cornstarch, salt, eggs, and pandan leaf to a blender and blend until smooth.
instructions.3: Pour the custard mixture into the pumpkin. Place the pumpkin in a deep pan filled with hot water, ensuring the water reaches halfway up the pumpkin.
instructions.4: Cover the pan and steam-cook over medium heat for 45 minutes or until the custard is set.
instructions.5: Let the pumpkin cool slightly before serving. It can be served hot or cold.

w-th-018.culturalNotes: Custard in a pumpkin is a traditional Thai dessert, often served on special occasions.

w-id-001.title: Apem Beras

instructions.1: Mix the yeast with sugar and warm water in a small bowl. Let it sit for 10 minutes to activate.
instructions.2: Blend the cooked rice and coconut milk until smooth. You can warm the mixture slightly in the microwave or on the stove until it is lukewarm (not hot).
instructions.3: Add the rice flour, cake flour, sugar, and salt to the mixture and blend well until the ingredients are combined.
instructions.4: Cover the batter and let it rest for 30 minutes in a warm place.
instructions.5: Pour the batter into apem molds and place them in a steamer. Steam for 30 minutes until cooked.
instructions.6: Let the apem cool slightly before serving.

w-id-001.culturalNotes: Apem is a traditional Indonesian sweet made from rice and coconut milk. It is usually served on special occasions.

w-id-002.title: Asam Pedas (Spicy Tamarind Fish Stew)

instructions.1: Prepare the fish: Clean the fish and cut it into large pieces. Rinse it well with water and let it dry.
instructions.2: Prepare tamarind juice: Place the tamarind block in a bowl and pour 360 ml of water over it. Rub it well until it dissolves, then strain the juice.
instructions.3: Grind the ingredients: Grind the shallots, garlic, ginger, candlenuts, sambal oelek, coriander seeds, turmeric powder, and galangal powder in a blender until it becomes a smooth paste.
instructions.4: Cooking: In a large pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the ground paste and stir for 5 minutes until it turns golden. Add the tamarind juice, water, lemongrass, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the tomato, okra, pineapple, and sugar. Bring the mixture to a boil again, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the fish and cook for another 10 minutes until the fish is cooked through. Add salt to taste.
instructions.7: Serve the Asam Pedas hot with white rice.

w-id-002.culturalNotes: Asam Pedas is a popular dish in Indonesia, known for its sour and spicy flavors. It is typically served with white rice.

w-id-003.title: Ayam Goreng Kalasan

instructions.1: Toast the spices in a small skillet over medium heat (no oil) for 2 minutes or until the spices smell fragrant. Transfer the spices to a blender or a tall jug that fits a stick blender.
instructions.2: Add the remaining Curry Paste ingredients to the blender and blend until smooth.
instructions.3: Pour the Curry Paste over the chicken in a ziplock bag or bowl. Toss to coat, then marinate in the fridge for 24 hours, up to 48 hours.
instructions.4: Before cooking, prepare the chicken for frying. Coat the chicken in cornflour / cornstarch and mix well.
instructions.5: Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium heat. Fry the chicken until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes per side.
instructions.6: Drain the fried chicken on paper towels. Serve hot garnished with chopped coriander leaves.

w-id-003.culturalNotes: Ayam Goreng Kalasan is a traditional Indonesian dish known for its rich and creamy flavor.

w-id-004.title: Fried Chicken in Sweet Butter Sauce (Ayam Goreng Mentega)

w-id-004-i1.name: medium-sized chicken
w-id-004-i1.standardAmount: 1 medium-sized chicken, cut into small pieces (12-16 pieces)

instructions.1: Season the chicken pieces with salt. Coat them with lemon juice and let them marinate for 15-20 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat the oil to about 180°C (350°F), and fry the chicken until it is golden. Remove the chicken from the oil and set it aside to drain.
instructions.3: Sauté the garlic and onion for a minute or two. Add the remaining sauce ingredients.
instructions.4: Stir fry for a minute and then add the chicken pieces. Toss to coat.
instructions.5: Serve the chicken hot with lime wedges.

w-id-004.culturalNotes: Ayam Goreng Mentega is a popular dish in Indonesia, known for its sweet and tangy flavor.

w-id-005.title: Ayam Kecap

instructions.1: Mix the chicken with salt and black pepper and marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the shallots, garlic, ginger, and bird's eye chili and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until the shallots become translucent.
instructions.3: Add the tomato, yellow onion, and green onion and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the kecap manis, ketchup, oyster sauce, honey, and water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the marinated chicken and simmer for 15-20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
instructions.6: Serve the chicken hot with rice.

w-id-005.culturalNotes: Ayam Kecap is a popular dish in Indonesia, known for its sweet and spicy flavor. It is usually served with rice.

w-id-006.title: Ayam Penyet Cabe Ijo

instructions.1: Wash the chicken and cut it into pieces. Place the chicken in a bowl with 600 g of water. Add minced garlic, grated ginger, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, ground coriander, galangal powder, turmeric powder, salt, and chicken powder. Let the chicken marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry the chicken until golden brown and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the oil and set aside.
instructions.3: In another bowl, mix the serrano peppers, minced garlic, lime juice, salt, sugar, and chicken powder. Mash the ingredients well until they form a smooth paste.
instructions.4: Heat the oil for stir-frying in a pan over medium heat. Add the paste and stir-fry for 5 minutes until it turns a dark green color.
instructions.5: Add the fried chicken to the paste and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until well combined.
instructions.6: Serve the chicken hot with white rice and cooked vegetables.

w-id-006.culturalNotes: Ayam Penyet Cabe Ijo is a popular dish in Indonesia, typically served with white rice and cooked vegetables.

w-id-007.title: Ayam Pop Padang

instructions.1: Mix the chicken pieces with lemon juice and let them marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: In a pressure cooker, place the chicken, coconut water, lime leaves, bay leaves, lemongrass, galangal, and ginger. Close the cooker and cook on high pressure for 20 minutes.
instructions.3: After cooking, let the pressure release naturally. Open the cooker and remove the chicken.
instructions.4: In a pan, heat 4 tablespoons of oil and fry the chicken pieces until golden brown. Set aside.
instructions.5: To prepare the chili sauce, blend the garlic, shallots, cayenne pepper, bird's eye chili, and candlenuts in a food processor. Add salt and sugar and mix well.
instructions.6: In a small pot, heat 1 tablespoon of oil and add the spice mixture. Stir for a minute, then add coconut water and tomato. Let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes.
instructions.7: Serve the chicken with the chili sauce and chicken broth.

w-id-007.culturalNotes: Ayam Pop Padang is a famous dish from Indonesian cuisine, known for its rich flavors and unique cooking method.

w-id-008.title: Ayam Rica Rica

w-id-008-i1.name: chicken thighs or drumsticks or wings

w-id-008-i9.name: lemongrass stalks
w-id-008-i9.standardAmount: 2 stalks (trim and cut into 3-4 inch pieces and bruise)

w-id-008-i17.name: kaffir lime leaves (cut into thin strips)

instructions.1: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, cayenne peppers, and Thai chili in a food processor until smooth.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat, then add the blended mixture and sauté for 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the chicken and sauté for 5 minutes until golden brown.
instructions.4: Add the water, tomatoes, lime juice, sugar, salt, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, and pandan leaves. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce has thickened.
instructions.5: Add the lemon basil (kemangi) if available, and simmer for an additional 5 minutes.
instructions.6: Serve the chicken hot with white rice.

w-id-008.culturalNotes: Ayam Rica Rica is a famous dish from Manado, Indonesia, known for its spicy and sour flavors.

w-id-009.title: Bakpia (Bakpia)

instructions.1: Prepare the filling: Mix the mung bean paste well.
instructions.2: Prepare the water dough: Mix 140 g of flour with sugar and salt, then add the melted butter and hot water and knead until the dough is smooth.
instructions.3: Prepare the oil dough: Mix 100 g of flour with oil and knead until the dough is smooth.
instructions.4: Combine the doughs: Mix the water dough and oil dough together and knead until the dough is well combined.
instructions.5: Shaping: Divide the dough into small balls, then flatten each ball and place a small amount of filling in the center, then cover the filling and shape into balls.
instructions.6: Cooking on the stove: Place the balls in a hot, oiled pan and fry until golden brown on all sides.
instructions.7: Baking in the oven: You can also bake the balls in a preheated oven at 180°C for 15 minutes.
instructions.8: Cool down: Let the bakpia cool before serving.
instructions.9: Storing: Store the bakpia in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days.

w-id-009.culturalNotes: Bakpia is a traditional Indonesian sweet, also known as Hopia. It is usually served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-id-010.title: Bandrek

w-id-010-i3.name: old ginger
w-id-010-i3.standardAmount: 100 gr (peeled and cut into thin slices)

instructions.1: In a medium-sized saucepan, add the spices, lemongrass, and pandan leaves.
instructions.2: Bring the mixture to a boil, then lower the heat and let it simmer gently until the spices and herbs release a wonderful aroma, about 20 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the palm sugar or coconut sugar and stir until it dissolves.
instructions.4: Close the lid and let it steep for another 15 minutes.
instructions.5: Strain the beverage into serving glasses.
instructions.6: Add 1-2 teaspoons of condensed milk to taste.
instructions.7: Serve immediately.

w-id-010.culturalNotes: Bandrek is a traditional Sundanese drink from Indonesia, typically served in glass cups.

w-id-011.title: Batagor (Fried Dumplings with Peanut Sauce)

w-id-011-i14.name: palm sugar
w-id-011-i14.standardAmount: 150 g (start with 75 g and adjust to taste)

instructions.1: Prepare the peanut sauce: Blend the roasted peanuts and garlic in a food processor until smooth. Add palm sugar, salt, water, and lime juice, and mix well. Adjust the taste as needed.
instructions.2: Prepare the tofu: Cut the tofu into small cubes.
instructions.3: Prepare the meat/fish paste: Mix the ground chicken or fish paste with tapioca flour, egg, minced garlic, salt, sugar, and white pepper. Mix well until the mixture is smooth.
instructions.4: Adjust the taste of the mixture: Taste the mixture and adjust the seasoning with more salt or sugar if needed.
instructions.5: Stuff the tofu and wonton skins: Place a piece of tofu in the center of a wonton wrapper and add a small spoonful of the mixture. Fold the wrapper to enclose the filling.
instructions.6: Steaming: Place the dumplings in a steamer basket and steam for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Frying: Place the dumplings in hot oil and fry until golden brown. Drain the dumplings on paper towels.
instructions.8: Serving: Serve the dumplings hot with the peanut sauce.

w-id-011.culturalNotes: Batagor is a popular dish in Indonesia, a combination of fried dumplings filled with meat or fish and tofu, served with peanut sauce.

w-id-012.title: Ayam Betutu Bali

instructions.1: Prepare the spice paste: Blend shallots, candlenuts, sambal oelek, Thai chilies, garlic, ginger, kencur root, turmeric, galangal, coriander, terasi, kaffir lime leaves, coconut oil, lemongrass, white pepper, salt, coconut sugar, and lime juice in a food processor until smooth.
instructions.2: Precook the vegetables: Sauté the shallots in coconut oil until golden, then add the spice paste and cook for 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Stuff the chicken with vegetables: Place the cassava leaves and cooked vegetables inside the chicken cavity.
instructions.4: Wrap the chicken and marinate: Wrap the chicken in banana leaves and then in aluminum foil, and let it marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: If using an Instant Pot: Place the chicken in the pot and add 2 cups of water. Set the high pressure for 40 minutes.
instructions.6: If roasting: Place the chicken in a preheated oven at 180°C and roast for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
instructions.7: Serve the chicken with sambal matah if desired.

w-id-012.culturalNotes: Ayam Betutu Bali is a traditional dish from Bali, Indonesia, known for its spicy and aromatic flavors.

w-id-013.title: Vegetable Biryani

w-id-013-i12.name: carrots
w-id-013-i12.standardAmount: 6 carrots (peeled and cut in large chunks)

instructions.1: Wash the basmati rice under cool water until the liquid is no longer cloudy. Soak the rice in a bowl of clean, cool water for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: While the rice is soaking, put 6 cups of water in a pot along with the whole spices and salt. Cover and gently bring to a simmer.
instructions.3: After 30 minutes, bring the simmering pot of water to a full boil. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot. Gently boil for 5 minutes. Strain the rice and spread it in a large platter to stop the cooking.
instructions.4: In a large heavy-bottomed pot, heat the ghee and fry the sliced onion until deep brown. Remove the fried onion with a slotted spoon onto a plate lined with a paper towel and set aside.
instructions.5: Fry the potatoes, cauliflower, and carrots in the remaining ghee until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
instructions.6: In the same pot, fry the minced onion and tomato until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, sliced green chili peppers, and the spices. Stir until well combined and fragrant. Cool slightly, then stir in the yogurt. Add the chopped vegetables and stir to coat in the masala.
instructions.7: Scatter the raisins on top of the vegetables, then spoon on the parcooked rice. Smooth the surface and drizzle with rose water. Drizzle on the melted ghee if you want a more indulgent biryani. Cover and cook over low/medium-low for about 45 minutes until the rice is cooked through.
instructions.8: Taste the rice to make sure it is cooked to your liking. Tip onto a large family-style platter, stirring gently to combine all ingredients as you go. Top with reserved fried onion, slivered almonds, and cilantro.

w-id-013.culturalNotes: Biryani is a popular dish in Indonesia, often served on special occasions and family gatherings. It is known for its rich blend of spices and fresh vegetables.

w-id-014.title: Steamed Cake (Bolu Kukus Mekar)

instructions.1: Cut the gula Melaka into smaller pieces. Place it in a saucepan with coconut milk over low heat and stir until the sugar dissolves. Let the mixture cool completely before using.
instructions.2: Mix the dry ingredients (flour, salt, baking powder) in a bowl and set aside.
instructions.3: Fill your steamer with water and start boiling the water. Make sure there is enough water to steam the cake for at least 15 minutes on high heat. Wrap the lid with a cloth to prevent water condensation from dripping onto the cake. Line the muffin cups with paper liners.
instructions.4: Prepare the cake batter: Beat the egg with granulated sugar until the mixture becomes creamy. Add the oil and mix well. Add the liquid mixture (gula Melaka and coconut milk) and mix well. Add the dry ingredients and mix until the batter is smooth.
instructions.5: Pour the batter into the lined muffin cups. Place the cups in the steamer and steam for 15 minutes on high heat.
instructions.6: Let the cake cool slightly before serving.

w-id-014.culturalNotes: Steamed cake (Bolu Kukus Mekar) is a traditional Indonesian dessert, often served on special occasions and holidays.

w-id-015.title: Bubur Cha Cha

w-id-015-i8.name: sugar
w-id-015-i8.standardAmount: 120 gr (about 1/2 cup + 5 tsp, or more or less to taste)

instructions.1: Wash, peel, and cut the sweet potatoes and taro into small pieces.
instructions.2: Place the sweet potatoes and taro in a steamer and steam for 15 minutes until tender.
instructions.3: In a separate pot, place the tapioca pearls in boiling water and boil for 10 minutes until they become translucent and chewy.
instructions.4: In a large pot, combine coconut milk, water, sugar, salt, and pandan leaves, and bring to a boil over medium heat.
instructions.5: Add the steamed sweet potatoes and taro, and the cooked tapioca pearls to the coconut milk mixture, and stir well.
instructions.6: Let the mixture boil for another 5 minutes, then turn off the heat.
instructions.7: Serve Bubur Cha Cha hot or cold, as desired.

w-id-015.culturalNotes: Bubur Cha Cha is a traditional Nyonya dessert, a mix of sweet potatoes, taro, and tapioca pearls in coconut milk.

w-id-016.title: Bubur Ketan Hitam (Black Sticky Rice Dessert)

w-id-016-i3.name: Water
w-id-016-i3.standardAmount: 800 ml (1000 ml if cooking on the stove)

instructions.1: Soak the black glutinous rice for 30 minutes if cooking on the stove.
instructions.2: Break the rice in a blender or food processor if desired.
instructions.3: Add the rice, water, coconut sugar, and pandan leaves to the pressure cooker.
instructions.4: Close the pressure cooker and cook on high pressure for 20 minutes.
instructions.5: After cooking, let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the coconut cream and salt, and mix well.
instructions.7: Serve the dessert hot or cold as desired.

w-id-016.culturalNotes: Bubur Ketan Hitam is a traditional Indonesian dessert often served on special occasions.

w-id-017.title: Cilok Bandung (Tapioca Balls with Peanut Sauce)

instructions.1: Prepare the peanut sauce: Blend the roasted peanuts, garlic, chilies, water, tamarind paste, palm sugar, Kecap manis, and salt in a blender until smooth. Cook the sauce over medium heat for 5 minutes until it thickens.
instructions.2: Prepare the tapioca dough: Mix tapioca starch, all-purpose flour, scallions, chicken powder, salt, sugar, and white pepper in a bowl. Gradually add the hot boiling water and knead until the dough is smooth and pliable.
instructions.3: Shape the dough into balls: Cut the dough into small pieces and shape them into small balls.
instructions.4: Boil the tapioca dough: Bring water to a boil in a pot and add the balls. Boil for 5 minutes until they float to the surface.
instructions.5: Serve: Pour the peanut sauce over the boiled balls and serve hot with your favorite chili sauce.

w-id-017.culturalNotes: Cilok is a popular dish in Indonesia, especially in Bandung. It is served as an appetizer or a light meal.

w-id-018.title: Pandan Kaya Swiss Roll (Bolu Gulung Kaya)

instructions.1: Spray a 9 x 13 x 1 inch baking pan with non-stick cooking spray or brush with oil, then line the bottom and sides with parchment paper.
instructions.2: Prepare the cake batter: Mix the egg yolks with the cooking oil and coconut milk until well combined. Add the flour and salt, and mix until the batter is smooth.
instructions.3: Prepare the meringue: Beat the egg whites with the sugar and cream of tartar (or lemon juice or vinegar) until stiff peaks form.
instructions.4: Fold the meringue into the cake batter gently until well combined.
instructions.5: Pour the batter into the prepared pan and spread evenly.
instructions.6: Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.
instructions.7: Let the cake cool slightly, then trim the four edges.
instructions.8: Make 4 shallow slits on the surface of the cake.
instructions.9: Spread the kaya jam over the surface of the cake.
instructions.10: Roll up the cake gently using the parchment paper to maintain its shape.
instructions.11: Remove the parchment paper immediately after rolling.
instructions.12: Serve the roll warm or cold as desired.

w-id-018.culturalNotes: Srikaya is a type of jam made from coconut milk and eggs, and it is popular in Indonesian and Malay cuisine.

w-id-019.title: Indonesian Chicken Curry (Kari Ayam)

instructions.1: Wash the chicken parts.
instructions.2: In a food processor or mortar and pestle, grind the garlic, ginger, candlenuts, turmeric, galangal, hot chilies (if using), and terasi into a paste (bumbu).
instructions.3: In a wok or skillet, cook the paste over medium heat for 1 minute.
instructions.4: Add the chicken parts to the wok, and brown them.
instructions.5: Add the shallots, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and salam leaves to the wok, and sauté for another minute.
instructions.6: Add the coconut milk and bring to a light boil.
instructions.7: Simmer on low heat for 10 minutes.

w-id-019.culturalNotes: Indonesian curry is a popular dish in Indonesia, known for its rich and complex flavors.

w-id-020.title: Dadar Gulung (Caramelized Coconut Pancakes)

instructions.1: Combine all the pancake ingredients in a large mixing bowl.
instructions.2: Whisk the ingredients well.
instructions.3: Strain the mixture if necessary to remove any lumps.
instructions.4: Heat a non-stick pan and brush with extra butter.
instructions.5: Ladle the pancake mixture into the pan until the bottom is thinly covered.
instructions.6: Flip the pancake when it is ready.
instructions.7: Repeat until the mixture is finished.
instructions.8: Place the water and sugar in a saucepan and heat until the sugar is dissolved.
instructions.9: Add the remaining filling ingredients and cook until all the liquid has evaporated.
instructions.10: Remove the mixture from the heat and discard the cooked pandan leaf.
instructions.11: Place equal portions of the filling in each pancake.
instructions.12: Roll the crepe into a parcel and garnish with fresh pandan leaves.

w-id-020.culturalNotes: Dadar Gulung is a traditional Indonesian dish often served as a breakfast or light dessert.

w-id-021.title: Stewed Pounded Cassava Leaves in Coconut Milk (Daun Ubi Tumbuk)

instructions.1: Wash the cassava leaves and cut them into small pieces.
instructions.2: Wash the pea eggplant and cut them in half.
instructions.3: If using dried shrimp instead of anchovies, wash them and soak in warm water until soft, then finely chop and set aside.
instructions.4: In a bowl, mix the shallots, garlic, red chilies, ginger, and turmeric, then grind until smooth.
instructions.5: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat, then add the ground spices and stir for 2-3 minutes until golden brown.
instructions.6: Add the kaffir lime leaves, torch ginger buds, and lemongrass, and stir for a minute.
instructions.7: Add the water and bring to a boil, then add the cassava leaves, pea eggplant, and anchovies (or dried shrimp), and stir.
instructions.8: Add the thick coconut milk, sugar, and salt (and chicken powder if desired), and bring to a boil over low heat for 20-25 minutes until the leaves are tender.

w-id-021.culturalNotes: Daun ubi tumbuk is a traditional Indonesian dish usually served as part of a lunch or dinner meal.

w-id-022.title: Dendeng Balado

instructions.1: Place all the ingredients for the spice paste in a food processor and process into a paste. Add a bit of water if needed.
instructions.2: Rub the beef with the marinade and let it marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Place the beef in a medium-sized pot. Add water just until it barely covers the beef and let it cook for about 45 minutes to 1 hour or until the beef is tender but not falling apart.
instructions.4: Remove the beef from the pot and let it cool down a little. Thinly slice the beef across the grain. Use a heavy object (such as a pestle) to pound the meat to about 1/4-inch thick.
instructions.5: Preheat a small to medium non-stick pan with about 1 Tbsp of oil. Pan fry the beef slices until they are lightly brown and dry.
instructions.6: Serve the dendeng with sambal.

w-id-022.culturalNotes: Dendeng Balado is a traditional Indonesian dish often served with rice and sambal.

w-id-023.title: Crab and Shrimp Egg Foo Young

instructions.1: Cook the proteins separately: In a pan, heat 1 tsp of sesame oil and sauté the minced garlic for 1 minute. Add the shredded carrot and sauté for 1 minute. Add the crab meat and chopped shrimp and sauté for 2-3 minutes until they turn white. Set aside.
instructions.2: Prepare the egg mixture: In a bowl, beat the eggs with 1 tsp of sesame oil, sugar, soy sauce, and ground white pepper. Add the cooked proteins and shredded carrot and mix well.
instructions.3: Cook the egg foo young: In a large pan, heat 1/3 cup of cooking oil over medium heat. Add the egg mixture and gently stir until golden brown. Cook in batches if necessary.
instructions.4: Make the gravy: In a small bowl, mix chicken stock, sesame oil, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and cornstarch. Pour the mixture into a pan over medium heat and stir until thickened.
instructions.5: Serve the egg foo young with the gravy and garnish with the green parts of the green onion.

w-id-023.culturalNotes: Egg Foo Young is a popular Chinese dish in Indonesia, often served as part of the Chinese-Indonesian cuisine.

w-id-024.title: Empanada Dough

instructions.1: In a medium bowl, whisk sugar and salt into the flour.
instructions.2: Using a pastry cutter (or two knives), cut the butter into the flour until it is pea-sized.
instructions.3: Add in water – a little at a time until a shaggy mass forms.
instructions.4: Press together with your hands. It will be a little dry to the touch. Shape into 2 flatted disks, wrap in saran and refrigerate while working on your filling.
instructions.5: After at least 30 minutes, remove dough from fridge and roll thinly, on a slightly floured work-surface.
instructions.6: Cut out shapes and fill (use a round cutter – either 3 1/2 or 5″ in diameter). Roll the edges to seal…
instructions.7: Now you can make beef empanadas or apple empanadas or… whatever your heart desires!

w-id-024.culturalNotes: Empanada is a popular dish in Indonesia, consisting of pastries filled with meat, vegetables, or fruits.

w-ir-001.title: Abgoosht (Persian Meat and Potato Soup)

instructions.1: Rinse the beans and drain them. Transfer the beans into the Instant Pot and add 2 teaspoons of kosher salt and enough water to cover the beans by 1 inch, about 6 cups of water.
instructions.2: Close the lid and seal. Set the Instant Pot to manual (or pressure cook on newer models) set to high pressure for 5 minutes. Allow for 20 minutes natural pressure release.
instructions.3: When done, drain the beans and discard the water. Reserve the beans.
instructions.4: Heat the Instant Pot to sauté on high and add 1 tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil.
instructions.5: Season the meat with 1 teaspoon of kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon of black pepper. Brown the shanks on both sides in batches, 3-5 minutes for each side. Once browned, transfer the shanks to a plate and reserve.
instructions.6: Add 1 tablespoon of oil to the hot pot then add chopped onions. Cook until softened then season with 1/2 teaspoon of kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric. Cook for 5 more minutes.
instructions.7: Start adding the shanks, chopped potatoes, and beans back into the pot with the onions.
instructions.8: Pierce the dried limes all over with a sharp knife and press them into the pot.
instructions.9: Whisk together tomato paste with beef broth then pour into the pot.
instructions.10: Close the lid and seal. Set the Instant Pot to manual (or pressure cook on newer models) set to high pressure for 35 minutes. Allow for 20 minutes natural pressure release.
instructions.11: Transfer the meat and bones to a large mixing bowl. When it cools, discard the bones and extra fat, leaving just the meat in the bowl. Shred with a fork.
instructions.12: Strain out the remaining solids from the broth. Reserve the broth. This is the cherished soup, abgoosht.
instructions.13: Some people serve the soup with the solids, but most mash the solids to make goosht koobideh.
instructions.14: Transfer all of the strained solids to the mixing bowl with the meat. Use a potato masher or food mallet to smash and press the solids into a paste. Add broth as needed, to smooth out the paste. It should have the consistency of Mexican refried beans. Adjust the seasoning to taste by adding more salt or more limoo omami (the powdered kind).
instructions.15: To serve the broth, fill a bowl with bite-size pieces of sangak or lavash then pour the broth in.
instructions.16: Serve the goosht koobideh with more bread, torshi (Persian pickled vegetables), radishes, and fresh herbs (sabzi khordan).

w-ir-001.culturalNotes: Abgoosht is a traditional Iranian dish often served at family gatherings and social occasions. It is typically served with bread, pickled vegetables, and herbs.

w-ir-002.title: Advieh (Persian Spice Mix)

instructions.1: Add all the spices to a bowl.
instructions.2: Stir the spices well to ensure they are evenly mixed.
instructions.3: Transfer the mixture to a tightly sealed jar.
instructions.4: Shake the jar well to ensure the spices are fully mixed.
instructions.5: Store the mixture in the spice cabinet and use it for rice dishes, stews, and kebabs.

w-ir-002.culturalNotes: Advieh is a traditional Persian spice mix used to enhance the flavor of dishes.

w-ir-003.title: Albaloo Polo (Sour Cherry Rice)

instructions.1: Soak the rice in a medium-sized bowl with water. Gently wash the rice by stirring it in the water with your hand. Pour out the water and repeat two more times. After washing the rice a third time, rinse and then cover with water and soak.
instructions.2: In a small bowl, combine the ground saffron with 1 tablespoon of hot water and set aside.
instructions.3: If using fresh sour cherries, clean and pit them. If using frozen cherries, thaw first.
instructions.4: Place the cherries and sugar in a saucepan and cook on medium-low heat for 15 minutes. Strain out the cherries.
instructions.5: Continue cooking until the juices are syrupy. Return the cherries to the syrup and remove from heat and reserve.
instructions.6: In a large non-stick pot, add 6 cups of water and 1 tablespoon of salt and bring to a boil. When the water has come to a boil, pour out the water in the bowl containing the soaking rice. Add the strained rice to the boiling water.
instructions.7: When the water comes to a boil again and the rice floats to the top of the pot (approximately 6 minutes), pour the contents of the pot into a fine colander.
instructions.8: Return the pot to the stove over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of butter and 1 teaspoon of saffron. When the butter has melted, add enough rice to cover the bottom of the pot. Mix with the saffron butter and gently spread flat in the bottom of the pot.
instructions.9: Scatter about 1/3 of the rice over this buttered layer. Spoon 1/3 of the sour cherries over the rice, using some of the syrup but not a lot. Repeat layering in rice and sour cherries until all the cherries and rice are in the pot.
instructions.11: Using the handle of a long wooden spoon, poke a hole down to the bottom of the pot. This allows the steam to escape.
instructions.12: Cover the lid of your pot with a clean towel or several paper towels, and set firmly over your pot to prevent steam from escaping. Reduce heat to low and continue cooking the rice for 45 minutes.
instructions.13: While the rice is cooking, prepare the meatballs. Mix the ingredients (except for the oil) together in a large mixing bowl. Scoop out enough meat to form a 1-inch meatball, approximately 20.
instructions.14: Once all meatballs have been formed, heat a large pan over medium-high heat and add oil. When the oil is hot, begin frying the meatballs until browned all over. This will take about 10-15 minutes.
instructions.15: Transfer the meatballs to a large bowl. Mix in 1-2 tablespoons of the reserved cherry syrup and coat the meatballs evenly.
instructions.16: When the rice is done cooking, scoop out about 1/2 cup of cooked rice and transfer to a bowl. Stir in the saffron water and mix until golden.
instructions.17: Scoop out the rest of the rice onto a serving platter and top with the saffron rice.
instructions.18: Break up the tahdig (crust) and place around the rice. Arrange the meatballs on the serving platter. Garnish with almonds and pistachios and serve.

w-ir-003.culturalNotes: Albaloo Polo is a traditional Iranian dish served on special occasions. It is known for its sweet and sour flavor from the cherries and saffron.

w-ir-004.title: Persian Barbari Bread

instructions.1: Place the flour, salt, sugar, oil, and yeast in the bowl of a stand mixer with a dough hook.
instructions.2: Turn the stand mixer on and set it on slow speed. Add the water slowly while the mixer is running.
instructions.3: Once the dough comes together, turn the speed to medium and knead for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Cover the bowl with a kitchen towel and let it sit for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Place the dough on a floured surface and divide it into two. Shape into balls and cover with a kitchen towel. Let the dough rise for 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Meanwhile, mix the glaze ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a simmer and stir until it thickens. This will take about 3-4 minutes. Set aside to cool.
instructions.7: After 30 minutes, place one of the balls on parchment paper. Flatten the dough using your hand into an oval shape. Using your fingers (except the thumbs) make indentations on the bread. Brush with the glaze and top with sesame seeds. Transfer the parchment paper to a baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap, and let it sit for another 20-30 minutes.
instructions.8: Preheat the oven to 225°C (440°F). Once the oven is hot, uncover the baking sheet and place the bread in the oven. Bake for 18 minutes until golden and cooked. Let it sit for 10 minutes before you slice it.

w-ir-004.culturalNotes: Barbari bread is a traditional Iranian bread known for its crispy exterior and soft interior. It is typically served with main dishes.

w-ir-005.title: Persian Yogurt Spinach Dip (Borani Esfenaj)

instructions.1: Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat and add olive oil.
instructions.2: Add onion and sauté until they start to soften.
instructions.3: Reduce heat to medium-low and cook until onions are slightly browned, about 7 minutes.
instructions.4: Add spinach and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, or until spinach is wilted and cooked. Remove from heat and let cool.
instructions.5: In a large bowl, add cooled spinach mixture with yogurt, salt, and pepper. Mix until combined, cover, and refrigerate for 2 hours prior to serving.
instructions.6: When ready to serve, transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with walnuts.

w-ir-005.culturalNotes: Borani is a popular dish in Iran, served as an appetizer or side salad.
